title: Saul, head and shoulders taller (1 Samuel 9–10)
hookLine: the first king is chosen, hiding among the baggage

lines: LOOKING FOR ANIMALS, FOUND A CROWN.
cards: A farmer's donkeys have wandered off. He sends his son and a servant to find them, and they search the hill country for three days. They're about to go home when the servant says: there's a man of God in the next town.
Maybe he can tell us where the donkeys went. So a tall young man walks into town looking for lost animals, and walks out a king. The man of God is Samuel, now grown old.
The young man is Saul. The Bible says there was no goodlier person among the children of Israel; from his shoulders upward he stood above everyone.

teach.b: Israel had asked Samuel for a king, to be like the nations around them, and the text treats it as a sad request: they're setting aside God as their king. God tells Samuel to give them one anyway.
Before Saul can even ask about the donkeys, Samuel tells him: they're found, stop worrying.
Then, privately, he pours a little vial of oil on Saul's head and kisses him. The Lord has anointed you prince over his people.
Anointed: in Hebrew, mashiach, the word English borrows as Messiah; Greek translates it Christ. At its start, it's simply oil on a nervous young man's head.
When Samuel first hints at greatness, Saul answers, in the Douay-Rheims: "Am not I a son of Jemini of the least tribe of Israel?" Benjamin, the smallest tribe. Then the public choosing.
All Israel gathers, lots are cast, tribe by tribe, family by family, and the lot falls on Saul. Everyone turns to look, and he isn't there.
In the Hebrew, the Lord's answer is: he has hidden himself among the baggage. The Douay, following the Latin, says only: "Behold he is hidden at home."
Either way, the man who stands taller than everyone is crouched out of sight.
They pull him out, and the people shout: "God save the king." A tender, almost funny beginning; the story will darken: Saul's reign ends in jealousy and tragedy.
But this week has been full of people who felt too small: Gideon in the winepress, Ruth the stranger, Hannah in tears, a boy in the dark. Saul makes one more.

how: Catholics hear the story of Saul's anointing in the weekday Mass readings, and the Church's own anointings, at baptism, confirmation and ordination with sacred chrism, carry on the old sign of oil poured on someone chosen.

o: the prophet who anointed Israel's first king
Israel's first king, found hiding when chosen
the small tribe that gave Israel its first king

games.q: the first king — tap the pairs.
p: why Saul went looking for Samuel

s: Saul went to Samuel hoping to become king
he went looking for his father's lost donkeys.
the Hebrew word for anointed is where Messiah comes from
when the lot fell on Saul, he stepped forward proudly
he couldn't be found. he had hidden among the baggage.

games.q: you're Saul. all Israel has gathered, and the lots are narrowing down tribe by tribe toward your family. what do you do?
o: slip away and hide among the baggage.
argue that Benjamin is too small a tribe.
games.why: he hides. the Lord tells them where, they bring him out, and he stands head and shoulders above everyone. the people shout, God save the king.

practice: Saul hid at the exact moment he was called. Think of where you duck out of sight when asked to stand up, busyness, jokes, your phone, letting someone louder go first, and notice it without judging.
Then picture stepping out, the way Saul finally did, and if you pray, ask for that courage.

wordCard.voice: Saul. Israel's first king, tall and frightened, anointed by Samuel and found hiding among the baggage. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: anointed. Samuel pours oil on Saul's head; the word comes into English as Messiah, and into Greek as Christ.

carryVoice: Your line: hiding in the baggage. And that's week fifty-seven: Gideon's fleece, Samson, Ruth on the road, gleaning, Hannah's prayer, speak, Lord, and Saul. Day three hundred ninety-nine, done.
